images.name: Spring in the Literature Club
images.description: Manuscripts, old club journals and a sea breeze await the next editing session on the old clubhouse's third floor.
images.background: The Literature Club keeps old journals and handwritten drafts in a third-floor room of the aging clubhouse. With too few members, it faces a merger review; its festival anthology, Spring Mint, carries the hope of remaining together.
images.storyContext: The room supports proofreading, interviews, shared work and quiet pauses. The illustration does not decide whether the anthology succeeds or the club keeps its room.
visualNotes: A worn table, blank manuscript sheets and a blue volume show the room's purpose.
Rooftops, cherry blossoms and the sea preserve the coastal spring setting.
The empty room's layout is an artistic interpretation, best shown uncropped in a gallery.

images.name: An Afternoon of Proofreading
images.description: Atmospheric vignette: Mio sorts festival anthology drafts, leaving the player's response and relationship open.
images.background: Mio is both class representative of 2-B and Literature Club president, accustomed to considering others first. Preparing the festival anthology gives her reason to share small tasks and remember work done together.
images.storyContext: This is a possible shared proofreading moment. The empty chair leaves a place for the player without assigning their appearance, a romance or a prior promise.
visualNotes: Mio retains the portrait's hairstyle, violet eyes and navy sailor uniform.
Offered pages, a pencil and an empty chair suggest an invitation to collaborate.
Window light, blossoms and sea maintain a wholesome everyday mood.

images.name: Mio Kamishiro
images.description: Mio holds books and papers against a dark sailor uniform, her shoulder-length black hair framing a gentle smile.
images.background: Mio is Class 2-B’s representative and Literature Club president. With the club under merger review, she carries responsibility for the Spring Mint festival anthology and the clubroom’s survival.
images.storyContext: For first introductions, class arrangements and club conversations. Her courtesy and smile do not establish an intimate relationship.
visualNotes: Books and manuscript pages identify her role; illegible pages are not a completed anthology.

images.name: Rin Asakura
images.description: Rin winks and smiles, with a flower clip in her reddish bob and a camera and interview notebook in hand.
images.background: Rin is a Class 2-B student and newspaper reporter. Interviews let her approach people; the festival’s rumor fact-check wall also makes the limits of publication part of her work.
images.storyContext: Her playful default portrait suits interview invitations and everyday conversation. The smile does not mean she already knows the player’s secrets.
visualNotes: Camera, notebook, armband and flower clip preserve her identity.

images.name: Kaho Shiina
images.description: Kaho winks with an acoustic guitar, long light-brown hair falling beside a cream cardigan and small hair ornaments.
images.background: Kaho is Class 2-A’s Light Music Club guitarist and is writing an unnamed song. Direct and seemingly casual, she takes the stage and those who listen to her practice seriously.
images.storyContext: Introduces rehearsals, stage preparation and after-school invitations. Neither the guitar nor the smile establishes a finished song or an agreed outing.
visualNotes: The acoustic guitar, cardigan and hair ornaments define the default design.

images.name: Yuma Shiraishi
images.description: Bespectacled Yuma wears a tidy uniform and holds a clipboard with a quiet, serious expression.
images.background: Yuma is a Class 2-C student and council vice president, responsible for club registration, budgets and festival procedures. He often expresses care through reminders and rules.
images.storyContext: For club registration and council business. The clipboard establishes no review result, and his serious expression does not imply hostility toward the player.
visualNotes: Glasses, striped tie and clipboard are his main identifying details.

images.name: Haruka Mikoeda
images.description: Haruka holds a blue folder, her long hair partly tied back and a council badge on her uniform, with a composed expression.
images.background: Haruka is the third-year student council president, coordinating festival resources and procedures. Gentle and precise, she brings disagreements back to practical arrangements.
images.storyContext: For budgeting, room allocation and festival coordination. Her authored role is supportive; the portrait adds no romance route or private promise.
visualNotes: Partly tied hair, council badge and blue folder preserve the original portrait.

images.name: Chihiro Onodera
images.description: Chihiro wears her hair in a low bun and a beige cardigan, holding up chalk while supporting an open book.
images.background: Chihiro is Class 2-B’s homeroom and language teacher and the Literature Club’s former adviser. She respects student autonomy and understands the pressures on small clubs.
images.storyContext: For the transfer student’s introduction, lessons and gentle guidance. She offers support while students make their own club choices.
visualNotes: Her adult face, chalk and book establish her role as a teacher.

images.name: Souta Morikawa
images.description: Souta raises a pair of drumsticks, smiling broadly in a rolled-sleeve white shirt and loosened tie.
images.background: Souta is the Light Music Club drummer and Kaho’s bandmate. Outgoing and quick to speak, he livens up a room but can cause misunderstandings by misreading silence.
images.storyContext: For ensemble scenes and stage preparation. His bandmate relationship follows the source; his smile adds no rivalry or romance.
visualNotes: Paired drumsticks, short hair and rolled sleeves identify the drummer.

images.name: Akane Toujou
images.description: Akane has long straight dark hair and holds a blue hardback with a purple floral detail visible beside it, her gaze quiet.
images.background: Akane is the third-year library committee chair and a regular at Umineko Bookstore. She values old publications and club memories, expressing care through seats, books and quiet company.
images.storyContext: She enters the story naturally when the player visits the library. The portrait does not presume a reserved seat for the player or a disclosure of family history.
visualNotes: The book and flower are visual details; the source does not establish the flower’s origin, giver or symbolism.

images.background: Class 2-B is the transfer student’s daily base, with the opening seat at the back beside the window. Duties, lunch, study and the Sea Breeze Post festival stall connect classmates.

visualNotes: Both views preserve three floors, right-side ivy and the sea on the left.

images.description: Cherry trees canopy the slope toward the seawall, with the school fence and gate on the left and a white vending machine on the right. Soft daylight illuminates the space.
images.background: The seawall connects the route home with pauses by the water, shared walks, waiting and conversations about lyrics. The town’s few after-school destinations make encounters and rumors likely to intersect here.

visualNotes: Left fence, right vending machine, seawall and paving keep their positions.

images.name: Seireki Town Shopping Street · Day
images.description: Books and flowers line the left side; tables and guitars appear in windows on the right, with colorful awnings, bicycles and the sea beyond. Soft daylight illuminates the space.

images.storyContext: The day view suits shopping for supplies, browsing books and meeting others. Storefronts convey the district without inventing names from indistinct signs.
visualNotes: Books and flowers remain on the left, food and instruments on the right, with the crossing and sea aligned.

images.name: Sea Breeze on Campus
images.description: Sunlight falls across a slope beside the school building, with cherry blossoms, green trees, campus roofs and the bay beyond the railing.
images.background: Haruka Academy stands on a gentle slope in coastal Seireki Town, its classrooms facing the harbor. With twenty-one days until the spring festival, a transfer student begins a new daily life in Class 2-B.
images.storyContext: For the homepage and world introduction, establishing the coastal campus, spring clubs and everyday relationships. The empty scene establishes no chosen club or romance.
visualNotes: This campus overview is distinct from the five authored scene anchors; distant buildings receive no invented story-location names.
